newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Command sees late rush on Cairn offer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Command sees late rush on Cairn offer.

text.p: Command Petroleum Holdings NL said on Wednesday it expected a late rush of acceptances for a takeover offer by U.K. resources group Cairn Energy Plc.
"I am confident it will go over 50 (percent) and end up somewhere between 50 and 90, I guess," managing director John Doran told reporters after Command's annual general meeting.
Cairn, which is offering $A1.10 for each Command share or a two-for-thirteen share swap, has about 42.2 percent of Command.
Doran said some shareholders would not sell "because they like the movie that is running". He said others were hoping for a rival offer but he held out little likelihood of another bid.
"It's unthinkable, which means it could happen but I can't think of it, that there will be a rival offer at this stage."
Doran said two other companies had conducted a due diligence on Command, whose major asset is a 25 per cent stake in the big Ravva oil and gas field offshore India in the Bay of Bengal.

Market sources told Reuters earlier this month that international oil firms Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and Hardy Oil and Gas Plc had looked at Command but could not improve on Cairn's A$354.5 million offer.
The Cairns bid has been recommended by Command directors.
Cairn's scrip offer expires on Friday, but the company earlier this month extended the cash alternative deadline to November 28.
Doran said Command's three board nominees from Snyder Oil Corp, which has accepted Cairn's offer for its 32.6 percent stake in Command, were expected to resign next week.

Command also said on Wednesday reserves at the Ravva field had risen to 210.3 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe), up from 190 mmboe previously. Doran said he expected recoverable reserves at Ravva to reach 230 million barrels of oil equivalent "sooner, rather than later".
